evidence.summary: Kernel run() output massively violates the contract tolerance across the legal domain: ordinary randn FP16 inputs at N=64/128/256 give max absolute errors of 15-64 (tolerance ~1e-4), with 273145 total violating components across cases including random, extreme-magnitude, bit-pattern, subnormal and impulse inputs. Output tensor properties (shape [B,N/2+1,2], FP32, contiguous, cuda, input preserved) are correct, but values are wrong. Reference is kernel.reference = torch.fft.rfft in FP64, which matches the contract formula.

rationale: The kernel uses a packed complex DIF radix-2 FFT plus post-reconstruction with a 64-entry cosine table; any indexing, twiddle-folding, or Nyquist-store error would violate the required abs(actual-exact) <= 1e-4 + 1e-6*abs(exact) tolerance for some legal finite FP16 input (widths 64/128/256, magnitudes up to 65504).

scope_evidence.summary: Contract requires X[b,k] = sum(values[b,j]*exp(-2*pi*i*j*k/N)) with abs(actual-exact) <= 1e-4 + 1e-6*abs(exact) for every legal finite FP16 input with N in {64,128,256}, including signed zeros, subnormals and both finite extremes; output must be fresh contiguous FP32 [B,N/2+1,2] on the input device.

scope_rationale: The contract requires the exact DFT values within 1e-4+1e-6|exact| for every legal finite FP16 input; a numeric or indexing failure on any such input violates the stated per-component tolerance requirement.
statement: The kernel's run() output deviates from the exact unnormalized forward real DFT beyond the tolerance 1e-4 + 1e-6*abs(exact) for some legal input in the contract domain (N in {64,128,256}, 1<=B<=256, any finite FP16 values).
